title: Voice Agents: the good, the bad, and the ugly
talk_summary: A CTO describes building an AI voice interview agent, starting with a monolithic prompt and progressively adding out-of-band text-domain side agents (drift detector, next-question agent, transcript-error filter) plus tool-use constraints to control behavior. He concludes that separate text-domain checker agents, tool calls as instrumentation, and LLM-judge evals over synthetic personas are the generalizable techniques.

takeaways.technique: Out-of-band checker agent on the transcript
takeaways.what_they_do: A separate text-only LLM call watches the conversation transcript and decides if the main agent is on/off track, then forces the main agent's tool call when it drifts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an additional background agent that's listening to the conversation and running a separate side thread to decide ... do we think we're kind of like off track or on track

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting the LLM free-form, they require it to call a tool to advance state, so the harness deterministically knows and controls what happens next.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Tool use can be very um powerful for constraining behavior and for getting uh sort of uh as a sort of a hack to instrument the llm

takeaways.technique: LLM-judge metric suite over synthetic personas
takeaways.what_they_do: They define per-attribute metrics (clarity, completeness, professionalism) each backed by a tuned judge prompt, and run them over synthetic conversations generated from a roster of LLM personas.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we ask an llm as judge to measure how clear was this conversation how complete was this conversation how professional was the agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of only the literal question, they attach high/medium priority goals explaining the 'why', so the model can rephrase and follow up sensibly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we added goals and priorities as a first class concept ... we're telling it the why behind the question

takeaways.what_they_do: They stopped stuffing the whole plan into one prompt; they feed one question at a time and inject targeted prompts when the user jumps around.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let's just ask one question at a time put that one question into the prompt that we're sending to the llm

takeaways.technique: Dedicated filter agent for noisy inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: A separate agent reviews transcript segments and hides likely transcription errors from the user while still passing them to the core model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: its entire task is should we hide this piece of the transcript from the user do we think we'd have a transcription error
